title: Run-level wall-clock limit — fix test failures and wiring gaps
goal: Correct all test failures, lint violations, and wiring gaps found after the first build pass so that npm test and npm run lint both pass and every acceptance criterion is verifiably met.

steps.description: Fix tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh: correct the bash syntax error at line 173 where an env-var assignment cannot prefix a subshell literal (use a wrapper or move the assignment inside the subshell); fix the lint-test-errexit violation at line 176 by replacing set+e/set-e with cmd||rc=$?; add a pipeline-state.json assertion checking disposition=misconfigured on the invalid-value path to satisfy SPEC-2.

Fix tests/unit/run-watchdog-clean-exit-test.sh: replace set+e/set-e blocks at lines 80 and 131 with cmd||rc=$? to pass lint-test-errexit; strengthen the SPEC-3 assertion to verify the watchdog PID no longer exists after the runner exits (kill -0 check) rather than only checking the abort sentinel is absent.

Fix tests/integration/run-timed-out-test.sh: replace set+e/set-e blocks at lines 137, 224, 273, and 334 with cmd||rc=$? to pass lint-test-errexit; make P2's inter-dispatch assertion falsifiable by checking a specific observable (e.g., first stage result exists but second stage was never dispatched) instead of assert_pass in both conditional branches; add persist assertions on every timed-out exit path, not only P4.

Fix tests/integration/resume-after-run-timeout-test.sh: replace the set+e/set-e block at line 133 with cmd||rc=$? to pass lint-test-errexit; add an explicit timing assertion making the SPEC-4 claim non-inferential — record the resume wall-clock start time and assert the run survives past the original run's remaining window before the watchdog fires.

Fix core/pipeline/runner.sh: add disown after spawning the watchdog background subshell so bash job-control does not block the runner's exit on the watchdog's 20700 s sleep — this is the root cause of the three pre-existing integration test timeouts; also ensure persist appears alongside release in the always_run fixture the integration tests use so all timed-out exit paths exercise both stages.

Fix core/pipeline/template.sh wiring: add an end-to-end test case in tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh that invokes the runner with a fixture template file containing max_run_s, asserts the resolved limit equals the template value, so that reverting template.sh causes the test to fail and the acceptance-gate reachability check passes.

Fix tests/unit/run-open-items-test.sh: update or add the run_end_words count assertion from 5 to 6 (the new timed_out arm in run-open-items.sh adds a sixth matching line, per the design supersedes block) so that reverting scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh causes the test to fail and the acceptance-gate reachability check passes.

Update tests/golden/full-pipeline/event-sequence.golden and tests/golden/parity/event-sequence.golden to include any new events emitted by the timed_out run path; regenerate both files using the project's golden-test infrastructure so the shape-floor check passes.

Verify docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md §11 Enforced by entries name test files that exist on disk so npm run lint passes; confirm config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt no longer lists ADR-054-stage-contract.md; these are doc-lint correctness checks, not new content changes.

open_questions: The issue acceptance criterion says 'ADR-054 §9 amended' but the build correctly added §11 because §9 already existed as 'Per-stage router configuration surface' — is the acceptance criterion using §9 as a draft placeholder for the new (now §11) section, or does it require §9 itself to be extended?

The three pre-existing integration test timeouts (core-pipeline-runner-test.sh, core-pipeline-strategy-test.sh, vision-admission-gate-test.sh) are attributed to the watchdog disown gap, but if those tests also hang after the disown fix the root cause may be a different process-group or fd-leak issue introduced by the watchdog subshell.
